document.title: Usama bin Ladin: Pressing High-Level Taliban Official Jalaluddin Haqqani on Bin Ladin (State 095538)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Secret, NODIS] U.S. officials meet directly with Jalaluddin Haqqani, Acting Minister of Borders, to discuss bin Ladin. Haqqani is described as a key official with links to Arab militants. He is appreciative of U.S. aid during the anti-Soviet jihad but resentful of the August 1998 missile strike on a Haqqani-linked camp in Khost. U.S. officials warn the U.S. will keep making things difficult for the Taliban unless bin Ladin is expelled. Haqqani agrees bin Ladin is 'a problem' but suggests the best solution is for him to remain in the country.

events.description: US cruise missile strike on Bin Ladin-linked facilities in Khost Province, which also hit Haqqani-linked facilities, a madrasa, and killed about 25 mujahideen.
US Embassy political officer met Jalaluddin Haqqani, urging the Taliban to expel Bin Ladin; Haqqani said Bin Ladin was under control and urged continued talks.
Embassy Islamabad cable 4099 reporting the meeting was sent and relayed by State as 095538.
US cruise missile strike on bin Ladin-linked facilities in Khost, destroying Haqqani's base and madrassah and killing 25 of his mujahideen.
US Embassy political officer met Jalaluddin Haqqani, first embassy meeting in over three years, urging expulsion of bin Ladin.
Islamabad cable 4099 reporting the Haqqani meeting was sent to State and repeated to posts.
Recent discussions between Taliban Deputy Foreign Minister Mullah Jalil and the US Charge on bin Ladin and other issues, with no progress.

key_claims: Jalaluddin Haqqani was the Taliban's acting minister of borders and a Kabul sector commander, with close ties to Arab and Kashmiri militants.
US officials judged that facilities linked to Haqqani, Bin Ladin's group and Kashmiri militants were hit in the August 1998 Khost strike.
Haqqani echoed the Taliban line that Bin Ladin was under tight control and that this might be the best solution.
Haqqani privately recognized that the Taliban's Bin Ladin policy was isolating them from the US and Saudi Arabia, and asked for continued talks.
Haqqani met US officials discreetly because the Taliban did not want him meeting foreigners.
The embassy noted Haqqani was concerned about further US military action after the Khost strike.
